_doc: Log-specific disruption scenarios for loan_model/disruptions.py (Phase 5). Mechanisms are generic (outage, routing_surge); this file maps them onto BPIC2017 stages, transitions and work items. All intensities are assumed and swept (Modules 2-3/Assumptions_Table.md section 3). Durations in hours; every shock lasts a length drawn uniformly from 72-120 h, which the agent never sees.

D1_offer_outage._doc: Offer dispatch system down: cases that finish the complete stage cannot get their offer sent.

D2_telephony_outage._doc: Contact-centre telephony down: call sessions cannot start.

D3_documents_surge._doc: Document portal fault: more validations find the file incomplete, and the customer's upload is held up by the faulty portal (upload_delay_h, wall-clock, added to the incomplete visit). Each case routed to incomplete during the surge is a decision.

D4_demand_spike._doc: Demand spike: applications arrive at arrival_factor x the normal hour-of-week rate (the hours that start during the spike). Nothing is blocked and at x3 the pool absorbs the work (sweep_demand_spike.py: almost no work item waits a working day); the harm comes weeks later, when the spike's cohort reaches its deadlines together and its usual share of slow customers misses them at once. So the decisions target those cases: see trigger.

trigger._doc: During working hours, a case that arrived during the spike, in a customer-facing stage, still on track and within slack_h of its stage deadline, gets one decision per stage visit (failure type overload).

sla_alert._doc: D6: a case blocked by a disruption and left waiting gets a second decision when its slack (stage deadline - age) falls to the threshold.

recovery._doc: Phase 6: recovery actions. All values assumed and swept (Assumptions_Table.md section 4). Costs are kappa x c_p (c_p = 1). Times in working hours for handling/retry (only working days and hours count), wall-clock hours for customer-side delays.

allowed._sla_risk: an SLA-risk alert allows the actions of the failure that blocked the case
allowed._retry: retry is not offered in an outage: a waiting case (do_nothing) resumes the moment the service is restored, so retrying could only resume it later and at a cost; it stays for missing documents (automatic re-fetch)

retry._doc: Missing documents only (masked in outages, see allowed._retry): an automatic re-fetch after delay_working_h finds the documents with documents_success_p, so the case skips the incomplete loop. At most max_per_case retries per case (then retry is masked).

offer_dispatch_outage._doc: send the offer through the online-only channel (O_Sent (online only), used for 4.9% of offers in the log); with rework_p the customer misses it and it has to be re-sent later

telephony_outage._doc: contact the customer in writing instead of by phone: the call is skipped but the customer responds later

overload._doc: automated written reminder (e-mail / text) to the customer: the remaining customer waits of the case's current stage visit shrink by wait_factor; no worker needed

escalate._doc: a backup worker does the blocked step by hand (offer sent manually, call from another line, file completed directly). The backup workers are real workers of the log: per work item, the team_per_item workers with the most sessions for it outside the constrained pool (the next ranks after the pool's); their qualification and attendance (active_day_share) are mined and they only take escalations. Escalate is masked while no backup worker for the step is on shift and free. Handling time and success probability are assumed: a manual workaround is slower than the logged system-supported session (0.3-2.7 min median). Demand spike (overload): a backup call-centre worker calls the customer personally; on success the remaining customer waits of the case's current stage visit shrink by chase_wait_factor.

reassign._doc: missing documents: a caseworker chases the documents directly (the case skips the portal delay) and the case's incomplete-file calls go to the front of the queue (fastest free qualified worker), ahead of other cases. Demand spike (overload): the case's remaining calls in its current stage go to the front of the queue.

training_cycle._doc: One cell per scenario, the length drawn per episode (72-120 h for every shock type). Short outages were removed: up to ~72 h they did about as much harm as normal day-to-day noise. D4 (demand spike) is defined but left out of the cycle: under the threshold-free Loss it adds only 0.03 +- 0.21 Q-days per episode (D1-D3 ~0.17), i.e. no measurable harm.
